title: A Five-Minute Pause Before You Respond
keyword: a five-minute pause before you respond
excerpt: A short pause before you reply can help you name the feeling, check the facts, and choose a response that matches what you actually want.
content:
Your phone lights up. A short message leaves you feeling rejected, and your fingers are already typing.

Before you press send, try this short pause. Five minutes is a suggested starting point, not a deadline for feeling better. You can take longer or use a different approach.

## Start by putting the message aside

If there is no urgent practical issue, place your phone somewhere nearby. Tell yourself: "I can answer after I've had a moment to think."

Waiting briefly does not commit you to accepting the message or ignoring the problem.

## Notice where you are

Feel your feet against the floor or your back against a chair. Look for three things you can see. Notice one sound around you.

If comfortable, breathe gently for a while. Do not force a large breath or hold your breath. If this feels unpleasant, return to noticing your surroundings.

## Name the feeling and check the facts

Try: "I feel disappointed and worried."

Then separate the message from your interpretation. "They said they can't meet tonight" is a fact. "They never wanted to see me" is a conclusion that needs more information.

You might still have good reasons for concern, especially if this has happened repeatedly. The pause helps you describe those reasons clearly.

## Choose the purpose of your response

Do you want information, a new plan, a boundary, or some time to think?

For clarity: "Do you want to reschedule?"

For a repeated problem: "This is the third cancellation. I need us to talk about whether we can make reliable plans."

If you remain too upset to write something you mean, save a draft and revisit it later. If another person is waiting on a practical decision, send a short acknowledgment and say when you can respond.

The pause is useful when it helps your next action match your purpose. It does not have to remove every uncomfortable feeling.
